Alas, anyone expecting even a fraction of the wit found in Edward Albee's similarly structured "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?" is bound to be sadly disappointed in Joshua Owen's "Human Things," now at the Theatre.
Human Things is the best kind of small play: intimate in scale, with extremely talented actors, ambitious in its questions.
With sharp comedic turns, Human Things turns a remote island, an approaching storm, and two troubled marriages into an affecting night of theater.
It is a worthy piece of theater worth the trek and your time.
It is drifting from start to finish.
The play is riveting- smart, imaginative and provocative.
Five-time Tony nominee Clark (The Light in the Piazza, Kimberly Akimbo) is a force to be reckoned with, delivering a master class in acting in the second half of the show, one you’ll not soon forget.

cn.t: Owen's debut receives mixed reviews, with critics praising Victoria Clark's standout performance and the play's ambition in tackling climate and relationships, but faulting its overstuffed themes and uneven execution.

vr.q: not bored, quite confused by this, but I did enjoy seeing this. I'm glad I saw it.
